text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ NYMEX crude and oil products seen entering a consolidative phase after Monday's late rally.
+ A hammer formation on yesterday's daily NYMEX crude chart seen a positive sign.
+ Crude may eventually target the $23.60/83 gap.
NYMEX crude and oil products are seen entering a consolidative phase Tuesday following a strong close last night, technical analysts said.
'It looks better after the way markets closed yesterday,' said Victor Yu, vice-president at Refco Inc. 'We're entering a consolidative phase...The impression is that the market was a bit oversold.'
He said a hammer formation on the daily NYMEX crude chart was a positive indication.
March NYMEX crude ended 23 cents higher at $22.46 a barrel on Monday. On ACCESS it last traded at $22.62.
On Monday before the late rally it had fallen to $21.65, the lowest for the spot contract since $21.50 was hit on August 27, and the first time it has traded below $21 since August 29.
Yu said that NYMEX crude could eventually work towards the $23.60-$23.83 gap left from Wednesday and Thursday's sessions.

'(Monday's) bounce took the oversold short term indicators off the boil, and improved the look of stochastics. For today, look again for consolidation with an upward bias, at least early on,' said Charles Gray of Prudential-Bache in a daily report.
'I think we have seen a short-term bottom,' he added.
MeesPierson Derivatives in a report said for March NYMEX crude they would 'stick to selling rallies to $22.85 or buying dips to $21.80 (in light volume unless products strengthen).'
March heating oil finished 1.23 up at 61.76 cents per gallon on Monday. On ACCESS it last traded at 62.10.
On Monday, March traded down to 59.55 cents, the first time the spot contract has been below 60 cents level since August 16.
Gray said that March heating oil has minimum resistance at 62.24/40 cents, having moved through the 61.40 pivot (the middle of Friday's range) on Monday, then the gap at 62.75/63.25 cents.
Yu sees pretty good support for March heating oil at 60.00 after the contract climbed back above that level on Monday.
March unleaded gasoline had settled on Monday 0.47 higher at 63.53 cents a gallon. On ACCESS it last traded at 63.75.
On Monday March traded down to 61.40 cents, the lowest since the low of 61.30 reached on October 1.
Yu said gasoline was the weakest of the NYMEX contracts, and saw as the eventual target the gap at 66.80/67.30 cents.
While unleaded gasoline recovered well on Monday, it still has pivot resistance at 64.33 (the middle of Friday's range) to contend with, warned Gray.
Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge Ltd said in a report that energy markets look oversold in the near term.

'But the longer term picture is continuing to threaten further falls so any rallies that develop from the test of current supports should be used to re-establish shorts, with stops just below the late January highs for now,' she said.
